why: B separates protocol parsing from execution and reuses one execute path for live commands and replay, whereas A mixes validation, phase checks and mutation in one large function and replays by building JSON strings and re-parsing them; B's derived phase (flags plus a nil active piece) is slightly implicit, but the structure is still easier to extend safely.

A separates parsing into a typed request from execution and has replay reuse the same execute path as live commands, whereas B mixes validation and execution in one function and replays by re-serialising JSON strings back through it, though A's implicit phase derivation is slightly fragile.

B models phase as an enum that owns the active piece, parses requests into typed Commands (replay becomes a validated command list before any state changes), derives level and hold_available instead of storing them, and has process-level protocol tests; A keeps string phases, mixes parsing with execution in one long stringly-typed function, re-serializes JSON to run replays, and uses a fragile -0 text hack.

A models phases and kinds as enums, parses requests into a typed Command, and runs replay through the same execute path with a thorough test suite plus end-to-end protocol tests, whereas B relies on stringly-typed phases and a command() that re-parses JSON and carries a byte-level '-0' hack, which makes it harder to extend safely.
